item.title: Shared HTTP busy resend
item.text: The shared HTTP client treats HTTP 429, 502 and 529 as busy responses. A busy request is resent unchanged until it has been sent max_sends times; max_sends is configurable and defaults to 5. When the limit is reached the client returns http.provider_busy. The holdoff between sends is applied in the runner queue.

anchor.statement: A request that receives an HTTP 429, 502 or 529 response must be resent until a configurable maximum number of sends, 5 by default, is reached.
anchor.scope: adds or changes busy-response handling, resend, holdoff or the runner queue

item.title: Shared HTTP busy resend
item.text: The shared HTTP client treats HTTP 429, 502 and 529 as busy responses. A busy request is resent unchanged until it has been sent max_sends times; max_sends is configurable and defaults to 5. When the limit is reached the client returns http.provider_busy. The holdoff between sends is applied in the runner queue.

Do not judge whether the item obeys, carries out, or breaks the anchor.

criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the behaviour the anchor statement governs or on an area named in anchor.scope, whether or not it mentions or follows the anchor's rule.
criteria.no: The item concerns a different component or activity; completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell which component or behaviour it touches.

anchor.statement: A request that receives an HTTP 429, 502 or 529 response must be resent until a configurable maximum number of sends, 5 by default, is reached.
anchor.scope: adds or changes busy-response handling, resend, holdoff or the runner queue

item.title: DecisionId newtype

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` gives a concrete rule: an action that must happen, the conditions that trigger it, and any limit or default. Does `item.text` state that rule's action together with its limit or default, in its own words or the statement's, as something the item will do? A mention of the topic, a promise to 'handle' it gracefully, or a goal without the concrete action does not count. Judge whether the rule's content is present only, not whether anything else in the item conflicts with it.

criteria.yes: The item states the anchor's required action and its limit or default as part of the plan.
criteria.no: The item is silent on the rule, names only its topic or a vague intent, or plans a different action than the one the statement requires.
criteria.unclear: The item states some of the rule's concrete content, but it cannot be told whether the required action itself is planned.

contradicted.instructions: List to yourself the concrete commitments `item.text` makes. Does any of them rule out what `anchor.statement` requires, or require something the statement rules out, for a case the statement governs? Omission is not conflict, and commitments about cases outside the statement are not conflicts. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: At least one concrete commitment in the item rules out what the statement requires for a case it governs.
criteria.no: No concrete commitment in the item rules out what the statement requires.
criteria.unclear: A commitment in the item might rule out the requirement, but it is too ambiguous to tell.

item.text: Busy responses (HTTP 429, 502 and 529) are resent until max_sends, configurable with default 5, is reached. Other errors such as HTTP 400, 401 and 500 are not busy responses and are returned to the caller immediately without resend.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` contain an explicit step, constraint, or design decision that performs the behaviour `anchor.statement` requires, including the limit or default the statement sets? Count only specific content; an item that merely mentions the same subject, or that does something else instead, does not carry the requirement. Judge presence only.

criteria.yes: An explicit step or constraint in the item performs the required behaviour with the statement's limit or default.
criteria.no: No step or constraint in the item performs the required behaviour; the item is silent, topical only, or does something else.
criteria.unclear: A step in the item may perform the required behaviour, but its wording is too loose to tell.

contradicted.instructions: List to yourself the concrete commitments `item.text` makes. Does any of them rule out what `anchor.statement` requires, or require something the statement rules out, for a case the statement governs? Omission is not conflict, and commitments about cases outside the statement are not conflicts. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: At least one concrete commitment in the item rules out what the statement requires for a case it governs.
criteria.no: No concrete commitment in the item rules out what the statement requires.
criteria.unclear: A commitment in the item might rule out the requirement, but it is too ambiguous to tell.

relevant.instructions: Compare `item.text` against `anchor.scope`, which lists the kinds of work this anchor governs, and against the subject of `anchor.statement`. Does the item do, or depend on, at least one kind of work listed there? An item that touches the subject while ignoring or contradicting the rule still matches. Judge subject match only.

criteria.yes: At least one piece of work in the item falls under anchor.scope or the subject of anchor.statement.
criteria.no: No piece of work in the item falls under anchor.scope or the subject of anchor.statement.
criteria.unclear: The item is too vague to tell whether any of its work falls under anchor.scope.
